commits.subject: Enable lazy startup for stdio MCP servers by default (#62366)
commits.reason: Adopt the stable upstream default for cached stdio MCP servers. A new chat can list cached tools without launching another optional process. Its first tool call starts the server. The explicit eager setting stays available.
evidence: The feature registry changes McpLazyStdioStartup from under development and disabled to stable and enabled. ALab has no packaged override. The earlier review of af9a98b074 kept the then-experimental flag opt-in.

Session startup selects DeferCachedStdio for an ordinary chat. The connection manager requires a matching usable catalog with an allowed tool, skips selected plugin servers, and keeps explicit reconnect eager. Required servers with live readiness still start eagerly. A required server configured for catalog readiness opts into deferral. Non-stdio transports keep their ordinary startup behavior.

The three changed test files exercise the default on a warm catalog, explicitly disable it for the eager PID control, and remove waits for optional processes in configured-identity and fallback-cwd cases. The existing scoped catalog and account-aware connection pool still determine reuse. The patch changes no live process transfer, model resolution, signed-update path or wire format.
commits.revisit: Run cached_stdio_stays_dormant_in_a_new_chat_until_first_use, code_mode_excludes_mcp_servers_using_their_configured_identity, and local_stdio_server_uses_runtime_fallback_cwd_when_config_omits_cwd against the merged source to qualify the default, eager override and first call.
